standard.title: Strategies to interpret culturally-loaded language
standard.description: develop strategies to interpret language that conveys cultural meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students recognise that language carries cultural meaning in social interactions and can identify culturally-specific expressions (AC9LCH2C04). They understand basic politeness and address conventions. They have not yet developed explicit translation strategies, used bilingual dictionaries, or analysed the risks of literal translation for culturally-embedded expressions and idioms.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop and apply strategies for interpreting language that conveys cultural meaning — including strategies for handling untranslatable expressions, formal and informal register, gesture and cultural symbols, and dictionary use for translation tasks.

nodes.label: Formal and informal register in context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain when to use formal and informal language in different social contexts, demonstrating appropriate language choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two contexts requiring different levels of formality in the target language and produce an appropriate language example for each.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish between formal and informal language in diverse social contexts — home, school, interactions with adults or authority figures; demonstrate appropriate language choices in context; compare language use across contexts and explain the social factors that determine register.
wider: Compare register conventions in the target language with English — identify where formal/informal distinctions map onto similar conventions and where they differ fundamentally
Analyse a short interaction text — identify the register signals (vocabulary, grammar, address forms) and explain what they reveal about the relationship between speakers
nodes.hinge_reason: Register awareness is the prerequisite for all culturally appropriate interpretation and production. Students who cannot distinguish formal from informal language cannot develop the culturally sensitive translation and mediation strategies the descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Register decisions require students to read the social context of an interaction and select language accordingly. Explicit discussion of the factors that determine register — relationship, setting, purpose — builds the analytical capacity before students can make spontaneous register choices.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two contexts requiring different register and explains why
Produces appropriate language examples for at least two different register contexts

nodes.label: Untranslatable expressions and cultural symbols
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify words and expressions in the target language that do not translate directly into English, explain their cultural meaning, and recognise cultural symbols and their significance.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two expressions or terms that cannot be directly translated and explain what each means in its cultural context.
nodes.typical_width: Identify culturally-specific terms and expressions — colloquialisms, culturally-embedded phrases, occasion-specific language — that resist direct translation; compare these with English equivalents or absence of equivalents; recognise cultural symbols and identify the language and values associated with them.
wider: Research a culturally-specific expression or symbol and create a bilingual explanation resource — explaining what it means, when it is used, and what it reveals about cultural values
Compare untranslatable expressions across two languages — identify whether they reflect fundamentally different cultural values or can be approximately explained

response_modes.reason: Untranslatable expressions are understood through varied cultural encounters — different occasions, relationships and contexts. Building a repertoire of examples across contexts gives students the cultural framework to approach new untranslatable expressions with strategies rather than confusion.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners are the class experts on culturally-embedded expressions — they carry this knowledge from home and community. Width investment in tasks that invite students to explain and teach culturally-specific expressions positions them as cultural authorities and deepens their own metalinguistic understanding.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two untranslatable expressions and explains their cultural meaning in context
Can explain why at least one expression cannot be directly translated into English

nodes.label: Translation strategies and dictionary use
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop and apply strategies for translating between the target language and English, including the use of bilingual dictionaries and awareness of translation limitations.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a bilingual dictionary to locate at least three words and produce a translation that accounts for context — not just the first entry.
nodes.typical_width: Use print and digital bilingual dictionaries to assist with translation; recognise that words can have multiple meanings depending on context; create bilingual resources — glossaries, picture dictionaries, signs — for classroom use; develop awareness of when and how to use translation tools.
wider: Translate a short text from the target language to English and explain at least two translation decisions — where a direct translation would be misleading and what approach was taken instead
Compare the output of a digital translation tool with a human translation of the same text — identify differences and discuss what the human translator understood that the digital tool missed

response_modes.reason: Translation strategies integrate register awareness (node 1) and cultural expression knowledge (node 2) into a practical mediation task. The teaching investment is in making explicit that translation is a cultural act — not a word-for-word substitution — through tasks that require genuine translation decisions.

success_criteria: Uses a bilingual dictionary to locate at least three words, selecting context-appropriate meanings
Produces a translation that accounts for context — not only the first dictionary entry
